title: Chapter 1 Quiz 3
description: The design process, the two kinds of error, and the parts of an algorithm.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Put the stages of designing a program in order.
questions.explanation: Problem statement, analysis, algorithm, coding (source program), compiling (executable program), running, result.

questions.question: Which stages are carried out **automatically by the machine**?
options: Translation of the algorithm into code
questions.explanation: Analysis and translation are intellectual human operations. Watch out: coding is human work. Only compilation and execution are done automatically.

questions.question: A program compiles and runs, but it prints 12 for 5 + 3. What kind of error is this?
questions.explanation: A semantic error comes from a poor design of the method, so the program runs but gives wrong results. Watch out: if it runs, there is no syntax error.

questions.question: The compiler cannot understand an instruction, so no executable program is produced. This is a…
questions.explanation: A syntax error is a spelling or grammar mistake made during coding. The compiler reports it and the program cannot run.

questions.question: A semantic error must be corrected starting from the analysis phase.
questions.explanation: Because it is a design fault, the algorithm itself must be corrected, beginning with the analysis.

questions.question: Put the parts of an algorithm in order.
questions.explanation: Name first, then the declarations, then the body: initialization, execution, and returning results.

questions.question: The name of an algorithm is always preceded by which word?
questions.explanation: Example from the course: ALGORITHM Factorial.

questions.question: The course writes: Avg ← grade1 * coef1 + grade2 * coef2 + grade3 * coef3 / (coef1 + coef2 + coef3). With grades 10, 14, 11 and coefficients 3, 2, 5, what value does a computer really calculate?
questions.explanation: The division is done first: 11 × 5 = 55, 55 / 10 = 5.5. Then 30 + 28 + 5.5 = 63.5. Watch out: the whole sum needs brackets, otherwise only the last product is divided. The weighted average needs (30 + 28 + 55) / 10 = 11.3.

questions.question: This algorithm should compute the weighted average of three grades. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Declare grade1, grade2, grade3, Avg As Real
Read(grade1, grade2, grade3)
Avg ← grade1 * 3 + grade2 * 2 + grade3 * 5 / (3 + 2 + 5)
Display(Avg)
questions.explanation: The brackets must cover the whole sum of products before dividing. Watch out: brackets around the denominator alone are not enough.

questions.question: A program that does not compile can still contain a semantic error.
questions.explanation: Syntax and semantic errors are independent. Watch out: a program with a syntax error cannot run, so the semantic error stays hidden until the syntax error is fixed.
